A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generative Blocks World. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations in Tables 1–2, qualitative editing comparisons, and appendix analyses of primitive density and vital layers.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds DragBench ablations, parameter studies, confidence intervals, and comparisons with commercial editing systems.

M1.justification: The convex-primitive extraction, depth-conditioned FLUX generation, correspondence-based texture hints, confidence masks, and inpainting procedure remain unchanged. Appendix Algorithms 1–2 match apart from formatting. The additional parameter studies do not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: v2 adds a reported DragBench evaluation for novel-view consistency in Table 4. LAION training, the original 48-image camera-move evaluation, and the overall camera/object-editing task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 9 adds actual qualitative comparisons against Reve, ChatGPT, and Gemini, substantially extending comparison methods beyond the retained research baselines. GoodDrag, FlowDrag, and Editable Image Elements appear in the related-work matrix but are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce LPIPS, quantitative component controls, and systematic sweeps of hint timing, LoRA weight, and mask dilation. The original Table 1 protocol remains unchanged. Figures 18–19 recommend t_end=300, while Appendix A.2 retains the default 500; this does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 quantitatively isolates texture-hint and StableFlow contributions. Figures 18–24 add timing sensitivity, depth-conditioning tradeoffs, dilation analyses, and additional DragDiffusion case studies. These substantially extend v1's predominantly qualitative component and parameter analyses; existing failure cases and vital-layer analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 20 newly reports 95% confidence intervals, and Figure 23 displays additional error bars. v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The revision does not specify interval construction, seed counts, or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical values. New DragBench results in Table 4 report PSNR 8.42 without hints versus 14.24 with hints; adding StableFlow gives 14.46 but reduces SSIM from 0.658 to 0.654. Parameter sweeps and additional comparative examples supply substantial new findings under their respective settings.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1 Section 3.2's explicit forward-noising definition and reverse scheduler-update equation. The convex geometry, back-projection, nearest-neighbor inpainting mathematics, and appendix algorithms remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of editable convex primitives at multiple scales, camera and object manipulation, texture preservation, and advantages over prior methods. The stronger emphasis on a 3D interaction paradigm and added supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit reasoning about shape constancy, contact consistency, and shape completion. New ablation interpretations explain the geometry–texture tradeoff and how dilation removes boundary misalignment. Existing limitations involving non-convex shapes, rotations, lighting, inversion, and video consistency largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a DragBench access link and describes interfaces and example prompts used for the commercial comparisons. Most architecture, hardware, timing, hyperparameter, and pseudocode details already appear in v1 and are retained or relocated to Appendices A.1–A.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds FlowDrag, GoodDrag, and Editable Image Elements, removes several background citations, and introduces Table 3's capability comparison. It also acknowledges 3D aspects of prior dragging methods more explicitly. These refine the existing positioning around editable primitives rather than replace its research context.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around 3D interaction and geometric consistency. Related work and discussion are condensed, generic diffusion exposition is removed, and technical details and hyperparameter selection move into structured appendix subsections. These are substantial narrative and organizational revisions.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison and ablation tables, heatmaps, uncertainty plots, and qualitative grids; expands Figure 4; and redistributes existing figures between the main text and appendix. Figure labels and captions are revised, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central texture-hint mechanism: Table 4 provides controlled quantitative ablations where v1 relied mainly on qualitative component comparisons. Figures 18–24 also test parameter choices and expose practical tradeoffs. These gains materially improve validation and guidance, despite unspecified confidence-interval construction and the unresolved t_end=500 versus 300 recommendation.
